findings.title: The runbook and the roadmap record Sentry rule 11 as BUILT in both projects; it exists in neither, and the rule ids are literal placeholders
findings.reason: The diff rewrites the rule 11 row from "REQUIRED BEFORE OWNER_OPERATOR_ENABLED GOES ON; NOT CONFIGURED BY THIS CHANGE" to "**BUILT 2026-09-12, staging rule `<staging-rule-id>`, production rule `<prod-rule-id>`**" — the row asserts BUILT while carrying unfilled placeholders where the file’s own convention (rule 9: "BUILT 2026-09-04, rule `3946648`") records a real id. docs/roadmap/2026-09-11-owner-operator/README.md:649 states BullMQ retry exhaustion "reaches Sentry ... under runbook **rule 11**, which Run B built in both Sentry projects before the staging flip", and README:697 says the decision was "closed as logs-only with rule 11 built in both Sentry projects". Read back from the Sentry API on 2026-09-12 (org repworth-nv): repworth-staging holds exactly two issue alert rules (3927243 solicitation-unattributed-suppression, 3608329 high-priority default) and repworth-production exactly four (3946648, 3927261, 3925256, 3920752). No rule matching agent-turn-exhausted, and no rule filtering subsystem:worker_job AND queue:agent_turn, exists in either project. The emitting half of the path IS present and correct (worker/job-failure-sink.ts:74 tags {subsystem:"worker_job", queue: queueName}; QUEUE_NAMES.AGENT_TURN === "agent_turn"), so this is the receiving half missing while three documents say it is in place — the intake names this exact alert as a go-live precondition ("First flip of OWNER_OPERATOR_ENABLED anywhere ... the Sentry rule-11 alert must exist before it") and .claude/CLAUDE.md carries the same owed item. Remedy: either build both rules and record their real ids, or revert all three claims to the REQUIRED/NOT CONFIGURED wording. Note that env-vars.md and eservices-variables.md state the precondition correctly, so the three claims above are the only false ones.

findings.title: The version-token fast-check property cannot distinguish a versionTokensEqual that ignores businessId
findings.reason: The property is titled "equal version tokens are exactly those with equal businessId and equal updatedAt text" and computes `expected = a.businessId === b.businessId && a.updatedAt === b.updatedAt`, but its generator draws updatedAt from fc.string({minLength:1,maxLength:40}). Two independently generated free strings are never equal in the default 100 runs, so the only pair that separates the real function from one comparing updatedAt alone — different businessId, SAME updatedAt — is never generated. Mutation M06 (drop the businessId comparison) passed the property. The example test at line 22 does cover the case, so production behaviour is pinned; the property is what is weak. Behavioural replacement: draw updatedAt from a small fc.constantFrom of two or three fixed timestamp strings (as businessId already is), so the cross product actually reaches equal-timestamp/different-row.

findings.title: markSiblingProposalsStale's `AND status = 'pending'` guard is unverified — deleting it kills no test
findings.reason: Mutation M11 removed the pending predicate from the sibling sweep and the live-DB case that exists for this sweep still passed. The fixture creates one pending sibling on the location, one pending proposal on a second location, and the proposal being applied — no ALREADY-TERMINAL sibling on the applied location, which is the only state the predicate decides. Without it, a previously APPLIED proposal on the same location is rewritten to status `stale` with failure_reason `version_mismatch` on the next Apply of that location, overwriting the applied record whose Receipt is still stored beside it — the state the intake’s Receipt invariant exists to prevent. Remedy: add one fixture row to the existing case — a second proposal on the applied location that is already `applied` (or `rejected`) — and assert its status and failure_reason are untouched after the sweep.

findings.title: `archived_at IS NULL` in the Apply businesses lock is pinned only by a SQL-text toContain, not by behaviour
findings.reason: Mutation M04 deleted the predicate and "applyProposal rejects the proposal location_not_found when the location was archived after preparation" still passed: that case primes an EMPTY lock result from the mock, so it proves the !locked branch, not the predicate that produces it. The only thing that catches the deletion is `expect(sqlCalls[1]!.text).toContain('archived_at IS NULL')` at apply.test.ts:174 — a string proxy for a behaviour, which passes for any query that merely mentions the phrase and would fail on an equivalent rewrite. The live-DB suite’s archival case applies FIRST and archives afterwards, so it exercises the repeat-Apply path, never pending-plus-archived. Behavioural replacement: one live-DB case that seeds a pending voice proposal, archives the location with the production helper, then applies — asserting rejected/location_not_found and that businesses is unchanged.

findings.title: catalog.ts writerFields is covered for set_tone only; the other three proposables have no test
findings.reason: `writerFields` is the new mechanism behind decision D10 ("only this operation’s own fields reach the shared voice writer"). catalog.test.ts never references it, and every Apply fixture — unit and live-DB — uses set_tone. set_products_services, set_avoid_facts and set_highlight_facts therefore have no test at all: swapping avoidFacts for highlightFacts in one closure, or returning {}, would write the wrong voice column or none, and the whole suite stays green. Remedy: a table-driven catalog case asserting, for each of the four proposables, that writerFields(parsed) returns exactly the operation’s own key with the parsed value.

findings.reason: RB-07 added `unsupported` to OwnerConversationTurn and a batched listUnsupportedForTurns. findings.title: readConnectionStatus is covered only for the never-connected (null) case
findings.reason: The only server-side assertion is `expect(summary.connectionStatus).toBeNull()` (reads.integration.test.ts:608). No vitest test seeds a zernio_connections row, so the latest-row rule (ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1, which is what makes a soft-deleted disconnect read as the current state), the JOIN businesses tenant scoping that stands in for the missing account_id column, the three accepted values and the "value no writer produces" throw are all unexercised. SummaryPanel.test.tsx covers the CLIENT rendering of the three values, which is a different question. Remedy: seed two connection rows for one location (an older `active`, a newer `disconnected`) and assert `disconnected`, plus one row on another account’s location asserting it is not read.

findings.title: A third impersonation-presence spelling survives the H1-B consolidation
findings.reason: Duty-4 sibling search. Patterns searched: `rw_impersonation`, `IMPERSONATION_COOKIE_NAME`, `hasImpersonationCookie` across src/ and worker/, excluding __tests__ and e2e/. Scope: every match, 26 hits. Result: the two byte-identical private copies the diff folded into the shared helper are gone, and all four operator/settings ROUTES now call it. One presence check remains hand-rolled — `Boolean(cookieStore.get(IMPERSONATION_COOKIE_NAME)?.value)` on the auto-approval server PAGE. It is not a defect: the shared helper takes a NextRequest and a server component has only `cookies()`, so the helper does not fit; recorded so the next consolidation does not report it as newly discovered. The remaining hits (admin/layout.tsx, admin/impersonate/[sessionId]/view/page.tsx, the impersonation start/end routes) read or set the raw value for verification, not as a presence gate, and are correctly untouched. Second pattern searched: nav arms below a `/dashboard` catch-all — `startsWith('/dashboard/')` across src/components and src/lib; two hits, active-nav.ts (the module the diff fixes) and protected-routes.ts (a flat allowlist with no fall-through order). ZERO siblings for that pattern.

findings.title: markSiblingProposalsStale's account_id predicate is behaviourally redundant (kept for ci:tenant-scope)
findings.reason: Mutation M13 removed the predicate and the live-DB sibling case passed. This is a provable non-defect rather than a coverage gap: businesses.id is globally unique, and every agent_proposals row has its account_id and location_id written together in buildProposalRows from one already-validated turn, so `location_id = L` already selects rows of exactly one account and adding `account_id = A` removes none and adds none. The predicate must stay — ci:tenant-scope requires it and it is the guard if a writer ever diverges — but no test can be written that would fail without it while the writer discipline holds. Recorded so it is not re-reported as an uncovered guard next round. No action.

findings.title: prevalidate-plan.py reports two stale commits in the handoff; both are fragments of a Codex session UUID
findings.reason: Duty 3 re-resolution. prevalidate-plan.py PASSES on the plan (97 citations, 16 fixtures, 1 commit), the deviations file (6 citations), the evidence file, the roadmap README and the runbook. It reports 2 issues on the handoff: `01a0960d` and `e1d2f82c8a0c` "do not resolve to a commit in this repo". Both are hex runs inside the Codex session id `01a0960d-4387-7f72-be06-e1d2f82c8a0c`, not commit references — a tool false positive, not a false claim. Recorded rather than silently dropped so the next pass does not re-investigate. No action.
